articles.title: Apex Legends Update Lets You Dual Wield the Wingman, Brings Back Lifeline Revive Shield
articles.summary: Some people are absolutely cracked with the Wingman. And now they’ll be able to use two at once. Cipher introduces Akimbo Wingman, which trades off some of the accuracy for big(ger) damage.
articles.body:
Apex Legends: Cipher is coming on November 3 and it’s bringing a new weapon style that makes me scared. The Wingman is a semi-automatic revolver that utilizes Sniper Ammo, and it’s been the bane of my existence since Apex Legends launched.

Some people are absolutely cracked with the Wingman. And now they’ll be able to use two at once. Cipher introduces Akimbo Wingman, which trades off some of the accuracy for big(ger) damage.

The Wingman has wavered a bit in recent seasons and sits as the 19th most effective weapon in DPS terms, but it’s still deadly in accurate hands, across basically any distance. It’s two-to-four headshots for a Wingman kill depending on the armor they’re wearing, which is what makes it so deadly in the right hands.

The Akimbo Wingman will push players in closer to barrel stuff your face. It’s going to be interesting to see where the weapon ends up with this new option — famously, the Akimbo Mozambique was famously nerfed quickly after it went from a barely used gun to the game’s dominant weapon.

On top of the dual revolvers, Crypto is getting a rework dubbed Crypto Rewired, which sees him role switch from a drone-camping git to a push-forward intel machine. His Surveillance Drone now runs on batteries instead of a cooldown, meaning it can be picked up and redeployed without a long wait, along with a new Sentry Mode that tags enemies on sight. On top of that, his EMP Ultimate can now be deployed with the press of a button.

Cipher also introduces Strongholds, which Respawn is calling the “evolution of care packages.” To access them you have to raid the Stronghold to haul out crate weapons, corrupted attachments, and EVO shield boosts for the squad. It’s a timely endeavour, and nearby enemies will hear the alarm.

Revenant and Lifeline are also getting buffs. For Rev, there’s a shorter Ult cooldown and faster Tactical, as well as new upgrades that allow him to extend his Ult with each knock. Another upgrade lets him Silence players with Shadow Pounce.

Lifeline is getting a reduced drone cooldown, self-healing while gliding, an Ult cooldown reduction, and improved flight mobility. On top of that, Respawn is bringing back her revive shield.

Elsewhere there are new Ranked updates, with Legend Bans in Diamond lobbies and above. Players vote to ban certain Legends, and the ones with the most votes can’t be picked for the match.

Apex Legends: Cipher launches November 3.

articles.title: Assassin's Creed Valhalla Is Getting New Game+ 6 Years After Release
articles.summary: Assassin's Creed Valhalla launched all the way back in November 2020, but Ubisoft just announced that it's getting its own New Game+ mode.
articles.body:
Assassin's Creed Valhalla launched all the way back in November 2020, but Ubisoft just announced that it's getting its own new game+ mode.

In a blog post, Ubisoft laid out some of its future plans for Assassin's Creed. One of them is a tiny, yet cryptic, update on Assassin's Creed: Codename Hexe . It also announced new game+ mode for Valhalla a mere six years after it first hit consoles.

The new game mode will be coming on November 5, and will include a new, optional progression mode, along with new runes, achievements and a stash system. Ubisoft will also be adding a new crafting material, Mithril, which can be used to upgrade divine gear.

Screens - Assassin's Creed: Valhalla -- Wrath of the Druids

But on top of the NG+ mode, Ubisoft teased that Valhalla will be getting even more updates. In the post, Ubisoft says it will "share full details in the upcoming Patch Notes, along with news regarding current-generation console updates in the coming days." It's not clear what Ubisoft means by "current-generation console updates," but I'd bet on a nice little graphics boost.

While Valhalla does have a PS5 and Xbox Series version, the game hasn't received a PS5 Pro Enhanced glow-up, so I'd guess that's what Ubisoft meant by console updates. But even outside of the Pro, in the years since Valhalla came out, every console has been updated with better upscaling, whether that's QSSR on the base PS5 or FSR 4.1 on the Xbox Series consoles.

Assassin's Creed was well received at launch. When IGN reviewed it, we gave it an 8, with reviewer Brandin Tyrrel saying, "Assassin's Creed Valhalla is a massive, beautiful open-world fueled by brutal living and the dirty work of conquerors. It's a lot buggier than it should be but also impressive on multiple levels."

The new game+ mode isn't the first time Ubisoft has slow-walked updates for Assassin's Creed Valhalla. Players also had to wait nearly two years to get Steam achievements , and the company was still fixing bugs with the game as late as January 2025.

articles.title: How to Get Rid of Radioactive Waste - Probably Stolen Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Radioactive Waste is a hazardous material that you can come across in Probably Stolen. There's a chance you might pick it up from the dumping ground, or
articles.body:
Radioactive Waste is a hazardous material that you can come across in Probably Stolen . There's a chance you might pick it up from the dumping ground, or customers could stop by to sell it to you, as they don't want to buy it to dispose of it. Regardless of how you get it, getting rid of it can be a hassle, and knowing what to do with it can be challenging, as no one explains it to you. Here's what you need to know about how to get rid of Radioactive Waste in Probably Stolen.

Radioactive Waste is special. Unlike other trash items, throwing it into your garbage can behind the counter won't get rid of it.

Instead, you need to bring it with you to the dumping ground and toss it there. To do this, place it inside a bag large enough to carry it, like a kid's backpack. Then, bring that backpack with you when you go out at night.

When you're at the Dumping Ground, remove the Radioactive Waste from the backpack and leave it on the ground. You can still proceed to attempt to scavenge for other materials when you're there, hopefully bringing something worthwhile back to you at the shop.

The real trick is making sure that you do this every few nights if someone has sold you Radioactive Waste. The only time you won't be able to do this is if you've suffered an injury. It does remove one customer from your expected queue, as you have to open up later in the day, but it's worth it to manage your shop's inventory.

Also, if you can't dedicate time to visit the Dumping Ground, keeping the Radioactive Waste in your shopkeeper's trash bin is an idea. The janitorial service won't take it away in the morning, but at least it won't take up your inventory space!

articles.title: Peng Meng, the Axemaster - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Peng Meng, the Axemaster is a story boss in Phantom Blade Zero. He appears near the end of the Against the Flow main quest, just outside the Outpost. He's
articles.body:
Peng Meng, the Axemaster is a story boss in Phantom Blade Zero. He appears near the end of the Against the Flow main quest, just outside the Outpost. He's the second story boss you encounter in Weeping Creek Valley. Here are a few tips and strategies for how to win this boss battle.

Peng Meng, the Axemaster, breaks free from his chains just as you arrive. He’s a large opponent with plenty of strong strikes, so prepare yourself. These are the special attacks you need to look out for in this fight:

The Axemaster is a slow-moving boss who hits extremely hard. Oftentimes, it’s safer to dodge than attempt a parry, but you’ll want at least a few successful parries to lower his Sha-Chi meter and cause a guard break.

The Axemaster has slow recovery animations after big hits, so stay patient and counterattack when he’s on the ground or regaining his balance. The Jagged Steel sword is great here because it inflicts Bleed and the boss is slow enough to give you generous combo openings.

You earn the Dread Axe after the battle. This is your first Phantom Edge – a secondary weapon that you can equip alongside your main weapons. You also automatically obtain a collectible titled The Axemaster’s Final Request .

articles.title: The Hunt, Hunter of the Order - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Hunt, Hunter of the Order is a story boss in Phantom Blade Zero, and he appears during the Steel and Steam main quest. He's the third and final story
articles.body:
The Hunt, Hunter of the Order is a story boss in Phantom Blade Zero , and he appears during the Steel and Steam main quest. He's the third and final story boss you encounter in Weeping Creek Valley. Here are a few tips and strategies for how to beat him.

How to Defeat The Hunt, Hunter of the Order

It’s time to settle the score against the Hunt in front of the Great Waterfall. This time, you’re fighting on solid ground instead of a moving cart. Some of his moves should feel familiar, but here are the special attacks you need to look out for:

The Hunt can attack from most ranges with wild chain sickle moves. Parrying will lower his Sha-Chi meter quickly, but if you’re not confident in the timings, just block until you see a blue or red flash attack. And switch weapons defensively to refill your Sha-Chi meter if it runs low while blocking.

Offensively, you can overwhelm the Hunt, especially if you obtained the Scarlet Wraithblade from the optional boss battle against Hua, Deadly Betrothed . It creates patches of Red Spider Lilies that drain the Hunt’s health if he stands in them during both Sha-Chi combos and Power Surges. And sometimes, a button prompt pops up during longer combos, giving you chances to deal extra damage.

The Hunt regains all of his HP once you fully deplete his health bar. This is phase two, against The Hunt, Sixfold Scythe . He now has extra arms that come with new attacks, so here are all of the new special moves that you should watch out for.

The Hunt has more arms in this phase, which means he has more sickles to launch your way. The attacks are a bit quicker and can hit you from a greater distance. He also has a slow-moving projectile that hits multiple times.

Your strategy doesn’t need to change much offensively – you can still overwhelm the boss. Just try not to overextend your combos, especially when you see the Hunt’s Sha-Chi meter refill.

You’re rewarded with the Hunter’s Chain Sickle Phantom Edge after the fight. It can perform long-range combos in battle, and it allows you to grapple onto high points outside of battle.

You can now access several new high points across the map to complete side quests and find rare items. The Hunter’s Chain Sickle can be used to grab the lost key for the Deep in the Valley purple quest, opening up the large area in the center of the map.

articles.title: Celeste and TowerFall Developer Explains Why Games Were Abruptly Delisted from Xbox
articles.summary: Celeste and TowerFall have been delisted from Xbox, as the developer has chosen to boycott Microsoft for its involvement and investments with the Israeli government.
articles.body:
Celeste and TowerFall have been delisted from Xbox, as the developer has chosen to boycott Microsoft for its involvement and investments with the Israeli government.

Developer Maddy Thorson, the mind behind Celeste and TowerFall, confirmed on Bluesky that her team had removed the games from Xbox. They are no longer available to purchase on the platform, which caught some fans by surprise. Thorson stated that she made the decision to remove the titles in support of the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement, which describes itself as a “Palestinian-led movement for freedom, justice and equality.” IGN has asked Microsoft for comment on the situation.

The movement targets companies that are involved with or invested in the Israeli government amidst the ongoing conflict between Israel and Palestine. Celeste and TowerFall are not the first games to drop Xbox as a result of this movement, either. Earlier this fall, the beloved co-op adventure game, Big Walk, chose not to release on Xbox and cited the boycott as its reason . The team noted that, should Microsoft divest from its Israeli ties and be removed from the list of BDS targets, Big Walk would be brought to Xbox.

"We have made the decision not to release Big Walk on Xbox, in accordance with the Palestinian-led BDS (Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions) movement’s call to boycott Microsoft, and their designation of Microsoft Games (and Xbox) as a priority boycott target," said Big Walk developer House House at the time. "If you need help understanding our motives, we would recommend reading about why Microsoft is a BDS priority target, the successes this kind of pressure has already had on Microsoft, and especially, watching this great introductory piece by People Make Games ."

Celeste and TowerFall have both been out for some time, with the latter having been released in 2013 and the former in 2018. Both games remain available for purchase on PlayStation, PC, and Switch.

articles.title: PUBG is Getting a Live-Action Series on Netflix Written, Directed by, and Starring Donald Glover
articles.summary: Yep, you read that right: Grammy-award winning music artist and actor Donald Glover is directing and starring in a live-action series adapting Krafton’s battle royale game, PUBG.
articles.body:
Yep, you read that right: Grammy-award winning music artist and actor Donald Glover is directing and starring in a live-action series adapting Krafton’s battle royale game, PUBG.

PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds is getting the Hollywood treatment with a TV show that will be written, produced, directed by, and starring Donald Glover. His brother, Stephen Glover, is also involved in the project as a co-writer and executive producer.

Other executive producers on the series include Michael Schaefer for NEON TV, Fam Udeorji for Gilga, and Taeseok Jang and Sujin Lee for LV3H. As told in a press release shared with IGN, Krafton — the South Korean gaming conglomerate that owns the franchise — is intent on expanding the IP into “original entertainment content.” LV3H, its entertainment entity, is also helping develop and produce the series.

While making an entire series based on a game where 100 players are dropped onto an island to fight to the death might seem like a bit of a stretch, there’s actually some pretty deep lore that explains the ‘why’ of it all. Admittedly, PUBG was initially created as a purely multiplayer experience, but it has since been fleshed out with an encompassing narrative that can be read on its official website.

The long and short of it is that the Battlegrounds are the brainchild of a billionaire named Sergei Kalimnik, who was the lone survivor of a deadly Soviet attack on the fictional island of Erangel in 1965. After experiencing “17 days of conflict” and watching Soviet officials attempt to dispose of their victims’ corpses, he came up with the brilliant idea of eventually buying the island and recreating his childhood trauma on a grand scale — conscripting 100 people and forcing them to fight until only one remains.

It’s sort of like Squid Game , when you think about it; these experiments expanded to other locales, while audience of shadowy, untouchable elites, much like the VIPs from Netflix’s hit South Korean thriller series, watch from afar. According to the PUBG Universe page, this also somehow ties back to a centuries-old tradition called ‘Magna Venari: The Great Hunt’ that began in the early 15th Century. Described as the “hunting of human prey,” it sought to answer a single question: “Why do some survive when others do not?”

There’s, surprisingly, a lot for Glover to work with here. And given his talents in showbiz ( Atlanta , Community, Swarm), I’m genuinely keen to see what he brings to the table from the PUBG world.

This is the latest video game to score a celebrity-led adaptation following news of Michael B. Jordan’s Battlefield movie . He, alongside Christopher McQuarrie, are reportedly shopping the adaptation around to different studios in hopes of bringing Electronic Arts’ popular military game series to the silver screen. Sony has emerged as a frontrunner to snag the film, though any other news remains nebulous for now.
